mechanism_narrative: A lower level of the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) directly reduces discount rates for equity valuations, generating positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as the cost of capital declines across the market.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 0.1%, or the Rank IC over 3-year rolling windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly CPIAUCSL increase exceeding 0.5 percentage points signals accelerating inflation, triggering Fed policy tightening expectations that depress equity valuations and produce negative S&P 500 forward 5-day returns.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in >55% of triggered periods (CPIAUCSL rise >0.5pp), or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous decline in unemployment (UNRATE < 5.0%) and rise in industrial production (INDPRO > 100.0) signals labor market tightness and supply chain strength, driving positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns through sustained corporate earnings growth.
regime_hint: labor market tightness with strong supply
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During monetary tightening cycles (FEDFUNDS > 2.0% sustained for 3 months), higher borrowing costs reduce corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 forward 20-day returns as equity valuations contract.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are positive in >55% of monetary tightening periods, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A higher level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates robust consumer demand, directly boosting S&P 500 forward 5-day returns through accelerated retail and manufacturing activity.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in >55% of periods when HOUST is above its 12-month moving average, or the Rank IC is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO < 95.0) signals manufacturing contraction, triggering negative S&P 500 forward 60-day returns as supply chain disruptions pressure corporate earnings.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are positive in >55% of periods when INDPRO < 95.0, or the Rank IC over 3-year windows is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent growth in housing starts (HOUST > 900.0) and retail sales (RSAFS > 425000.0) signals strong consumer spending, driving positive S&P 500 forward 20-day returns through elevated corporate revenue growth.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in >55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: During labor market recovery (UNRATE declining and PAYEMS rising for 3 months), improved employment conditions boost consumer spending, generating positive S&P 500 forward 60-day returns as earnings growth accelerates.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE declines and PAYEMS rises for 3 months
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in >55% of labor market recovery periods, or the Rank IC for the interaction term is below 0.03.
